step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard diagram depicts a pre-paid utility payment and management architecture on AWS. At the top right, a mobile device communicates with an ELB (Elastic Load Balancing) instance, which forwards requests to a central EC2 application instance. A retailer box ('R') sends real-time notifications to the mobile device and submits transaction business rule validations to the central EC2 instance. The central EC2 instance communicates with a utility backend ('UTIL'), which in turn communicates with the home meter ('M'). At the bottom layer, a database cylinder ('DATABASE') connects to a database EC2 host instance ('EC2'), which backs up data directly to an Amazon S3 bucket ('S3').
